problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 24 m³, revenue $272
* Container 2: volume 46 m³, revenue $254
* Container 3: volume 38 m³, revenue $30
* Container 4: volume 36 m³, revenue $104
* Container 5: volume 44 m³, revenue $224
* Container 6: volume 41 m³, revenue $112
* Container 7: volume 18 m³, revenue $14
* Container 8: volume 41 m³, revenue $189
* Container 9: volume 1 m³, revenue $173
* Container 10: volume 22 m³, revenue $60
* Container 11: volume 42 m³, revenue $108
* Container 12: volume 6 m³, revenue $288
* Container 13: volume 25 m³, revenue $31
* Container 14: volume 25 m³, revenue $157
* Container 15: volume 16 m³, revenue $74
* Container 16: volume 36 m³, revenue $60
* Container 17: volume 23 m³, revenue $295
* Container 18: volume 14 m³, revenue $106
* Container 19: volume 42 m³, revenue $276
* Container 20: volume 27 m³, revenue $92
* Container 21: volume 28 m³, revenue $19
* Container 22: volume 18 m³, revenue $138
* Container 23: volume 6 m³, revenue $11
* Container 24: volume 29 m³, revenue $161
* Container 25: volume 18 m³, revenue $197
* Container 26: volume 3 m³, revenue $224
* Container 27: volume 49 m³, revenue $26
* Container 28: volume 40 m³, revenue $31
* Container 29: volume 13 m³, revenue $10
* Container 30: volume 10 m³, revenue $54
The vessel has a maximum capacity of 546 m³. Choose the container combination that yields the highest total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
